If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast slope in mid-horizon (days 10–20) by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast slope in early horizon (days 1–5) by 5–10% to compensate for downward momentum.  
When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 5 days, shift forecast peak to later horizon (days 15–25) and reduce amplitude by 10–15%.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add a 3–5% downward bias to late horizon (days 20–30) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is consistently bullish but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast peak by 10–15% in mid-horizon and shift peak to later days to align with sentiment decay.  
If sentiment is bearish and price is rising, increase forecast decline rate in early horizon by 5–10% to reflect sentiment-driven reversal risk.
